title: The Three-Dimensional Human Skin Reconstruct Model: a Tool to Study Normal  Skin and Melanoma Progression
protocol: Mix 0.59 mL of 10X EMEM with reagents on ice.
Add 50 μl of 200mM L-glutamine to the mixture.
Combine 0.6 mL of FBS into the mixture.
Include 120 μl of 7.5% Sodium bicarbonate in the mixture.
Stir in 4.6 mL of bovine collagen I with other components.
Transfer 1 mL of the prepared mixture into each insert of tissue culture trays.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature to solidify the gel.
Centrifuge trypsinized human fibroblasts collected from flasks using 0.25% trypsin/EDTA.
Neutralize with DMEM containing 10% FBS.
Collect cells by centrifugation after neutralization.
Resuspend 0.45 x 106 cells in 1.5 mL of DMEM with 10% FBS.
Tap flask to detach dermal spheres formed from stem cell medium.
Centrifuge the collected dermal spheres containing 6600 dermal spheres.
Mix the following in a 50 mL tube on ice: 1.65 mL 10X EMEM, 150 μl 200 mM L-glutamine, 1.85 mL FBS, 350 μl 7.5% Sodium bicarbonate, 14 mL bovine collagen I and 1.5 mL fibroblasts suspension.
Add 3 mL of the mixture to each acellular layer-coated insert.
Incubate for 45 min at 37 °C in a 5 % CO2 tissue culture incubator.
After the gel solidifies, add DMEM containing 10% FBS (2 mL inside and 10 mL outside of insert in each well of skin reconstruct trays).
Incubate for 4 days and make sure that the gel contracts.
Aspirate medium from both inside and outside of each insert.
Add washing medium (HBSS with 1% dialyzed FBS) 2 mL to the inside and 10 mL to the outside of insert in order to wash off regular serum.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37 °C.

Mix 490 mL keratinocyte serum-free medium, 1.8 mL bovine pituitary extract, 10 mL dialyzed fetal bovine serum, 500 μl of 10 μg/mL SCF, 562.5 μl of 4 μg/mL bFGF and 500 μl of 264 μg/mL ET-3 to make basic medium (500 mL).
Add 10 μl EGF of 100 μg/mL to 100 mL basic medium for Medium I.
Add 2 μl EGF to 100 mL basic medium for Medium II.

Mix 72.5 mL DMEM, 24 mL F12 (HAM's), 2 mL L-glutamine of 200 mM, 200 μl hydrocortisone of 269 μg/mL, 200 μl ITES of 500X, 200 μl O-phosphorylethanolamine of 0.05 M, 200 μl adenine of 90 mM, 200 μl progesterone of 2 nM, 240 μl CaCl2 of 1 M and 100 μl chelexed newborn calf serum to make Medium I (100 mL).

Mix 72.5 mL DMEM, 24 mL F12 (HAM's), 2 mL L-glutamine of 200 mM, 200 μl hydrocortisone of 269 μg/mL, 200 μl ITES of 500X, 200 μl O-phosphorylethanolamine of 0.05 M, 200 μl adenine of 90 mM, 200 μl progesterone of 2 nM, 240 μl CaCl2 of 1 M and 100 μl newborn calf serum to make Medium II (100 mL).

Mix 142.5 mL DMEM, 142.5 mL F12 (HAM's), 6 mL L-glutamine of 200 mM, 600 μl hydrocortisone of 269 μg/mL, 600 μl ITES of 500X, 600 μl O-phosphorylethanolamine of 0.05 M, 600 μl adenine of 90 mM, 600 μl progesterone of 2 nM, 720 μl CaCl2 of 1 M and 300 μl newborn calf serum to make Medium III (300 mL).

Mix 0.5 mL of F12 (HAM's) with the specified volumes of L-glutamine, hydrocortisone, ITES, O-phosphorylethanolamine, adenine, progesterone, CaCl2, triiodothyronine, and newborn calf serum to prepare the final solution.
Trypsinize human keratinocytes from culture flasks with 0.05% trypsin/EDTA.
Neutralize trypsin with soy bean trypsin inhibitor (250 mg/L in 1x phosphate buffered saline).
Spin down the cells.
Resuspend a cell pellet at 4.17 x106 cells/mL in skin reconstruct medium I.
Trypsinize human melanocytes or melanoma cells from culture flasks with 0.05% trypsin/EDTA.
Neutralize trypsin with soy bean trypsin inhibitor.
Spin down the cells.
Resuspend a cell pellet at 0.83 x106 cells/mL in skin reconstruct medium I.
Remove washing medium from both inside and outside of each insert.
Add skin reconstruct medium I (1.5 mL to the inside and 10 mL to the outside of each insert).
Take 600 μl cell suspension of keratinocytes.
Take 600 μl cell suspension of melanocytes or melanoma cells.
Mix well the two suspensions.
Dispense 200 μl mixed cell suspension drop by drop to the inside of each insert.
For dermal stem cell reconstruct, use 100 μl of keratinocyte suspension only.
Incubate for 2 days at 37 °C.
Aspirate skin reconstruct medium I from both the inside and the outside of each insert.
Add skin reconstruct medium II (2 mL to the inside and 10 mL to the outside).
Incubate for another 2 days at 37 °C.
Aspirate skin reconstruct medium II from the inside and the outside of each insert.
Add 7.5 mL skin reconstruct medium III to only the outside.
Change medium III every other day until day 18.
Harvest skin reconstruct at day 18.
Aspirate media from inside and outside of inserts.
Remove inserts from tray with forceps.
Cut out reconstruct (including polycarbonate filter) by tracing a circle close to edge with scalpel blade.
Cut reconstruct and filter in half on hard surface.
Place one half of reconstruct in histology cassette between black TBS biopsy papers.
Soak cassette in 10% formalin for more than 4 hours.
Store cassette in 70% ethanol at 4°C until ready to process for paraffin embedding.
Place other half of reconstruct in 50% sucrose at 4°C for 1-2 hours.
Change sucrose to 2M and store at 4°C for another 1-2 hours.
Dispense optimal cutting temperature (OCT) into disposable base mold until it fills about 50% of boat.
Avoid any bubbles in OCT.
Remove reconstruct from sucrose using forceps.
Place on Kimwipes until sucrose is absorbed.
Transfer reconstruct into base mold on top of OCT using forceps and spatula.
Cover top of reconstruct with more OCT until base mold is completely full.
Avoid any bubbles in OCT.
Place base mold evenly on crushed dry ice.
Allow OCT to freeze completely.
Wrap the base mold in tin foil.
Store the wrapped base mold at -70°C until ready to use.
Prepare a 50 mL falcon tube with 5 mL of DMEM for freezing and defrosting mouse skin.
Anesthetize the female SCID hairless outbred mouse around 6 weeks old using isoflurane (4% in induction chamber, then 1.5-2% via nosecone).
Maintain mouse body temperature using a heated pad during anesthesia.
Apply sterile ophthalmic lubricant to prevent ocular injury.
Warm water in a beaker on a hot plate to maintain a temperature between 40 - 60°C.
Clean the mouse skin with compound benzoin tincture and alcohol prep swabs.
Mark a line on the top of the mouse back for suturing orientation later.
Cut a round wound bed about 1.2 cm in diameter using Iris scissors and forceps.
Cover the wound bed with sterile gauze sponges.
Place the round mouse skin in 5 mL of DMEM.
Freeze the tube containing mouse skin by placing it in a liquid nitrogen container until completely frozen.
Defrost the tube in hot water on top of a hot plate until totally thawed. Repeat this process three times.
Detach the skin reconstruct from the transwell using a surgical blade carefully.
Remove the membrane from the skin reconstruct very carefully.
Transfer the skin reconstruct (epidermis side up) onto the wound bed.
Place the mouse skin on top of the skin reconstruct with epidermis side up.
Make the first suture at the previously labeled marker.
Make a second suture at the bottom marker.
Suture two more stitches on each side to fix the mouse skin in place.
Clean the mouse skin after grafting is complete.
Remove the nosecone from the mouse.
Keep the mouse on a heated pad until it is awake and able to move around freely.
Transfer the mouse to a new cage once fully recovered.
Administer Meloxicam (1 mg/kg) by subcutaneous injection immediately post-surgery.
Repeat Meloxicam administration 24 hours after surgery.
Administer another dose of Meloxicam 48 hours after surgery.
Culture the dermal compartment in DMEM with 10% FBS for the first four days.
Switch to skin reconstruct medium I when keratinocytes are seeded with melanocytes or melanoma cells.
Expose the epidermis to air at day 9 to allow keratinocytes to differentiate.
At day 18, observe that the epidermis of skin reconstructs is composed of stratified keratinocyte layers.
Stain the section of reconstructs with the melanocytic marker S100 to show melanocytes are aligned in the basal layer and communicate with multiple keratinocytes through dendrite extensions.
Observe that the dermal compartment contains fibroblasts embedded in a collagen type I matrix.
Deposited collagen IV indicates the basement membrane, which separates the epidermis from the dermis.
Embed dermal stem cells labeled with GFP lentiviral vector with fibroblasts in a collagen I matrix to observe migration and differentiation into melanocytes.
Calibrate the shelf of incubator.
Use undifferentiated keratinocytes at lower passages.
